payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Change the image into pencil drawing
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is there image-grounded evidence of any progress toward rendering the content as a pencil drawing, even if the transformation is incomplete?
node.criteria: Pass if the image shows some visible pencil-drawing-style treatment of its content, including an incomplete treatment; fail if sufficient evidence shows no requested transformation has progressed; unknown if evidence is insufficient to determine whether any such progress occurred. Unrelated edits do not count as progress.
node.binding: Assess only visible changes in the supplied image that move its visual content toward a pencil-drawn style; do not infer progress from unrelated changes.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image shows a visible pencil-drawing-style treatment: colors are muted and the food and surrounding objects have sketch-like shading and outlines compared with the source.
The edited image shows a visible pencil-drawing-style treatment across the scene, with muted colors, grainy shading, and sketch-like outlines on the food and surrounding objects.
The edited image shows a visible pencil-drawing-style treatment: colors are muted and the food, dishes, and tableware have softened, sketch-like shading and texture compared with the source.

The edited image has a visible muted, grainy, pencil-like treatment across the food and surrounding objects, indicating progress toward a pencil drawing, though it retains substantial photographic color and detail.

The edited image has a visibly muted, gray-toned, grainy treatment across the food and surrounding objects, with softened, sketch-like shading consistent with some progress toward a pencil-drawing style.

fulfillment: The node’s completion criterion is too permissive and unstable: several traces call the image complete based on muted tones, grain, and sketch-like shading, while another identifies substantial photographic color/detail and correctly treats it as partial. The edited image shows clear pencil-like progress, but retains photographic lighting, texture, and object detail; do not equate desaturation or grain alone with the whole image reading as a completed pencil drawing. Keep the existing distinction between progress and completion, and make the whole-image check explicitly weigh whether the scene is recognizably rendered as a drawing rather than a photo with a pencil-like filter. Require evidence for that judgment, not merely repeated support passes, and preserve unresolved status when the whole-image evidence is unavailable. The transport failure is an execution/evidence-availability issue, not negative visual evidence; do not count it as a failure. Repeated variation warrants tightening the criterion, but the reference label is aggregate guidance, not atomic ground truth.
s3: Tighten the binding so the node independently judges the edited image’s overall visual identity, not just whether pencil-like cues are present across many objects. The edited image clearly shows progress—muted color, grain, and softened outlines—but retains photographic lighting, texture, and detailed food forms, so those cues alone do not establish completed pencil-drawing rendering. Require the evidence to distinguish a scene that reads as a drawing from a photograph with a pencil-like filter, and to cite both drawing-like qualities and any remaining photographic appearance before deciding pass or fail. Preserve the existing partial-progress distinction and use unknown only when the visual evidence cannot be assessed; do not treat the transport failure as negative evidence. Repeated high-confidence passes despite this ambiguity indicate the completion criterion needs clearer application, not that confidence or the requested style should be weakened.

The supplied edit has clear pencil-like shading and softened outlines across the scene, yet retains photographic lighting, texture, and detailed food forms. Thus it supports progress, not by itself completion; do not make this support check decide the aggregate completion label. Preserve fail for sufficient evidence of no requested progress and unknown for insufficient visual evidence. Treat transport or dependency failures as unavailable evidence, not negative visual evidence. Repeated high-confidence passes indicate criterion ambiguity, not a reason to weaken the requested style or infer absence from low confidence."}
